subject.title: [Bug]: project-local .env is ignored in 2026.3.28, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH falls back to ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

question: Should workspace `.env` be allowed to set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, or should project-local config selection remain limited to trusted process/global env and documented shell invocation?
rationale: Current main intentionally treats workspace `.env` as untrusted and blocks the full `OPENCLAW_` runtime-control namespace; changing that would alter a startup security boundary, not just repair a parser bug.

options.title: Keep Workspace Block
options.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` blocked from workspace `.env` and document shell/global `.env` as the supported per-project override path.

options.title: Allow Narrow Config Exception
options.body: Permit a constrained `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` workspace exception only with security review, focused tests, and docs for the trust model.

options.title: Adopt Linked PR Direction
options.body: Use the open linked fork PR as source material if maintainers accept its trust-boundary model and resolve its conflict/ownership blockers.

recommendation.title: Keep Workspace Block
recommendation.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` blocked from workspace `.env` and document shell/global `.env` as the supported per-project override path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current boundary appears to originate in their merged cwd dotenv hardening work, so they are the best history-backed routing candidate for the decision.
